questions: If there are multiple ways to make all 1s contiguous with the same minimal number of swaps, does the choice of which 1s move to which positions matter for the count, or is the answer uniquely determined regardless of which contiguous block we target?
Are swaps allowed only between adjacent characters, and does each swap count as one operation regardless of the characters swapped?
If there are multiple 1s, must they end up in exactly one contiguous block, or could they be split into separate contiguous blocks as long as each block is internally contiguous?
Does the answer depend on the order in which swaps are performed, or is it simply the sum of distances each 1 must move to reach the target block?
When moving 1s to form a contiguous block, can 1s cross over each other during swaps, and if so, does that affect the count?
Is the input guaranteed to be a string of exactly N characters, with no extra spaces or newlines, and N given on the first line exactly as described?
If there are multiple minimal solutions, do we need to output the number of operations for any one of them, or is the minimal number unique?
Should the output be just the integer answer, or should it include any extra text or formatting?
